name: – Nicolás Pascual de la Parte – § 49 – Am 140
title: REPORT on the implementation of the common security and defence policy – annual report 2024
part_text: 49. Recalls that the exclusive competence over foreign, security and defence policy belongs to the Member States with article 24(1) of the TEU stipulating that the EU cannot adopt legislative acts on foreign affairs and defence, and, thus, lifting the requirement for unanimity should not be considered; recalls that the EU Treaty framework already allows a number of different institutional forms of cooperation in the field of foreign, security and defence policy; reaffirms that any attempt to remove unanimity requirements in decisions related to defence, foreign, and security policy contravenes the spirit of the EU Treaty, as these domains are strictly within the competence of the Member States; reiterates that lifting the requirement for unanimity or shifting decision-making to a qualified majority system would undermine the cohesion and, by extension, the credibility of the EU on foreign policy issues; stresses that the qualified majority system would disproportionately favour the security interests of larger Member States, to the detriment of smaller Member States, despite the fact that, in the current security context, the latter are significantly more exposed to external threats;
